title: The Senate's own page says cloture on most matters takes three-fifths of all senators duly chosen and sworn
summary: The Senate's own page says cloture on most matters takes three-fifths of all senators duly chosen and sworn.
body: The Senate's page on filibusters and cloture says the number of votes required for cloture on most questions is three-fifths of all senators duly chosen and sworn, or 60 of the 100-member Senate. The source says: "senators voting to three-fifths of all senators duly chosen and sworn, or 60 of the 100-member Senate." The page states the cloture threshold used in a 100-member Senate. It is the Senate's account of its procedure. A different threshold for a particular question would have to be read in the rule that governs that question.
